#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Following up on this - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126510#issuecomment-2265947469

This PR helps improve the Job controller performance in sync path 

With this change, I have seen at least the update event handler sync path for job controller performance p99 increased by at least `128X` for cluster with `10k+ jobs`.

Cluster with similar load for Job Update event handler number w/o this change has `p99 13.02 ms` (vs) cluster w similar load for Job update event handler w this change has `p99 0.1024ms` i.e 12600% faster.

issue_context.title: The event handlers of job controller are slow
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

The event handlers in job controller are much slower than other controllers. It can cause the ring buffer in the processorListener to grow unbounded when the job churn is high enough.
The processing logic in the job controller events handler appears to be more complicated than other controllers. e.g. in [updateJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dbc2b0a5c7acc349ea71a14e49913661eaf708d2/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L464-L504), it invokes function `cleanupPodFinalizers` that lists the pods matching some selectors and the enqueue them to another queue. Similarly in [deleteJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dbc2b0a5c7acc349ea71a14e49913661eaf708d2/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L508-L524).

I added some instrumenting code to understand the latency of each event handler.
For job controller P99:
job add event handler: 0.080 ms
job update event handler: 3.075 ms
job delete event handler: 3.076 ms
pod add event handler: 0.136 ms
pod update event handler: 0.709 ms
pod delete event handler: 0.405 ms

For ttl-after-completion controller P99:
job add event handler: 0.0065 ms
job update event handler: 0.024 ms

The above 2 controllers processes same amount of job objects.

### What did you expect to happen?

Complicated logic should not be in the job controller event handler. They should be in the reconciler instead.
So that the event handler can be faster and pendingNotification can be drained faster.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I use a few thousands of cronjobs with TTL after completion.
I will add more details.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

1.30

@mengqiy thanks for reporting the issue. 

To help triage the issue I traced down the introduction of `cleanupPodFinalizers` code:
- for the `deleteJob` it was introduced in 1.24: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108752
- for the `updateJob` it was introduced in 1.29: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119944

The `updateJob` seems to be expensive only when finished Jobs are updated.

Given we only run one single goroutine for `run()` which is responsible for invoking the event handler https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dbc2b0a5c7acc349ea71a14e49913661eaf708d2/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go#L802
this can easily be the bottleneck in a controller whenever the event handler is slow.
The event handler that used by the informer is expected to be very thin and fast. It seems `cleanupPodFinalizers` has some expansive logic and slow down updateJob and deleteJob. 
IMO we should move `cleanupPodFinalizers` to the reconciler. User can easily increase the numbers of goroutines in the job controller by using higher `--concurrent-cron-job-syncs` to increase the parallelism.

```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  generateName: simple-
  namespace: kube-stress
spec:
  schedule: "* * * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 2
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 2
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 30
      template:
        spec:
          automountServiceAccountToken: false
          containers:
            - name: simple
              image: busybox
              command: ["sleep", "10"]
              resources:
                requests:
                  cpu: 5m
```

@alculquicondor @mimowo  FMU I already see we are handling the cases where `Job no longer exists` or `Job is in finished state` for a given pod in `delete pod event`  [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a1f0fc8f72441ce501142d9d6a86ecbe19c9b55b/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L421-L436) , I think we could safely remove `cleanupPodFinalizers` i.e [this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a1f0fc8f72441ce501142d9d6a86ecbe19c9b55b/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L522) from `deleteJob`  as it seems to be redundant ? It matches my understanding - we can drop `cleanupPodFinalizers` from `deleteJob`, as the finalizers will be removed when handling `deletePod`. WDYT @alculquicondor ?

Still, it would be good to make sure we have an integration test (either pre-existing or new). To check if there is an existing test you could delete the block of code in `deletePod`, after you make all tests passing after dropping `cleanupPodFinalizers` from `deleteJob`.

We added `cleanupPodFinalizers` in `deleteJob` precisely because we found complex cases where we were leaving Pods with finalizers.
IIRC, one race condition was when deleting a job and its pods in cascade. If the pod delete event arrived first, then the job still existed, so the pod is not orphan at this point. Then the job delete comes in and there might not be another event to resync the pod.

We do have integration tests for this, but the flakiness level tends to be very low when a bug exists.

I really don't think it's worth removing the additional `cleanupPodFinalizers`.
